newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's NSW 10-month budget surplus A$165 mln.
newsitem.headline: Australia's NSW 10-month budget surplus A$165 mln.

text.p: The Australian state of New SOuth Wales (NSW) has posted an underlying budget surplus of A$165 million for the first 10 months of the 1996/97 fiscal year (July-June), Treasurer Michael Egan said on Tuesday.
This compares with a surplus of A$359 surplus for the same period last year. In the 1997/98 budget delivered in May, Egan forecast a 1996/97 underlying surplus of A$67 million.
The NSW Treasury said the headline surplus of A$139 million comprised a current account surplus of A$1.555 billion and a A$1.416 billion capital account deficit.
The headline result compared with a A$350 million surplus for the same period last year. In the budget, the 1996/97 headline surplus was forecast at A$119 million.

"The turnaround in the April result between last year and this year is predominantly due to an increase in the level of current payment soffset in part by increased revenue from taxes, fees and fines and an increase in advances repaid to the budget," the Treasury said.

The underlying budget position excludes extraordinary items from equity restructures and the sale of government business enterprises. The headline result incorporates all transactions of the budget sector.
